actions.action: Slide the plant out of the pot and check the roots
Repot into fresh, well-draining cactus mix with extra perlite and trim dead or mushy roots
Bottom-soak the pot for 20–30 minutes if the soil is hydrophobic
Water only when the top inch of soil is dry and empty the saucer
Move to bright indirect light away from heaters and drafts
Apply dilute fertilizer once new growth appears
Take healthy segments, let them callus, and root them in light mix as backups
Post a photo of the roots if they look rotten or the plant is still limp after 2–3 weeks

reason: The answer attributes the limpness mainly to severe drying out with old compacted soil as a contributor. Its main advice is to repot into fresh mix and water when the soil is dry, which matches the repot the poster said worked, and nothing it recommends is harmful.
